SMTO-EML-0029 — Your email provider's sign-in service is temporarily down

GUID: c5392c98-bf1a-57d7-8988-739b06a6c9c3
Slug: email-smtp-auth-temporarily-unavailable
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • The mail server said it couldn't check the sign-in right now because of a temporary problem on its side. Your password wasn't rejected, and no email was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a few minutes. If your email provider has a status page, check it for problems. The server reported a short-term problem on its own side.
  2. Ask SMTO in a conversation to test the connection for this sender. A test checks the sign-in again without sending a real email.
  3. When the test succeeds, ask SMTO to send the email again. The sign-in failed before sending started, so this email did not go out.

What success looks like

  • The connection test reports success, and the email is then accepted by the mail server.

If it still fails

  • If it still fails after about an hour, send the copied error details to your email administrator. Don't change your password because of this error; the server didn't reject it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SMTP AUTH returned reply 454 (temporary authentication failure); credentials were not rejected and no message was transmitted.

What this means

  • The SMTP server returned reply 454 for a temporary authentication service failure. Classification uses the SMTP reply or negotiated capability, never the server response prose.

Why this can happen

  • The SMTP AUTH exchange returns the structured temporary-service reply 454.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Treat 454 as a transient provider-side failure: check the provider's status and rerun email.test_connection with backoff within the existing retry policy. Do not rotate credentials because of 454; escalate to the mail administrator if it persists.
  • Wait for the mail service to recover, then test the connection within the existing retry policy. Do not change the password solely because of this reply.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
